HOW IT WORKS
From URL to actionable report in under a minute

No setup, no signup. Paste a website URL or a listing from one of seven supported stores — we render it, score it across six categories, and rank what to fix first.

01
Paste a URL

Drop in any public homepage, landing page, pricing page, App Store or Google Play listing, Chrome Web Store extension, Shopify App Store app, GitHub repository, Notion template, or GPT Store listing. We auto-detect the type and render it in a real headless browser, JavaScript and all.

02
AI runs the analysis

Six categories — UX, content, performance, accessibility, SEO, and conversion — against a structured rubric, with the rubric reframed for the platform: ASO for app stores, install-conversion for Chrome and Shopify, README and star-conversion for GitHub repos, listing optimization for Notion templates and GPT Store agents.

03
Review prioritized fixes

Get an overall score, per-category breakdowns, strengths and weaknesses, and recommendations tagged critical, high, medium, or low. Export as PDF or re-audit later to track progress.

WHAT GETS SCORED
Six categories, one consistent rubric

A 0–100 score per category, with example findings drawn from the rendered page. Every supported listing type uses the same six categories, with SEO reframed as the right kind of optimization for the platform — ASO for mobile app stores, install conversion for Chrome and Shopify, star and clone conversion for GitHub READMEs, listing optimization for Notion templates and the GPT Store.

UX

Information hierarchy, task clarity, navigation, and visual structure.

EXAMPLE FINDING

"The hero buries the primary action under three lines of marketing copy — pull the URL form above the value prop."

Content

Copy clarity, depth, audience fit, and how well the page explains itself.

EXAMPLE FINDING

"~990 words but most of it restates the rubric. Replace with concrete example findings and outcome metrics."

Performance

Load behavior, page weight, and signals that affect perceived speed.

EXAMPLE FINDING

"286 KB response, 9.7s fetch — 8 scripts on a no-image landing page is too heavy. Defer non-critical JS."

Accessibility

Semantic structure, image alt coverage, language attributes, and form labeling.

EXAMPLE FINDING

"lang attribute set, viewport correct, 0 missing alts (no images). URL form is missing a persistent visible label."

SEO

Title, meta, canonical, headings, Open Graph, JSON-LD, and content depth.

EXAMPLE FINDING

"Title 58 chars (optimal), description 142 chars (optimal), canonical present but not self-referencing — fix the canonical URL."

Conversion

CTA prominence, trust signals, social proof, and friction in the primary action.

EXAMPLE FINDING

"One CTA, no social proof, no pricing or privacy reassurance near the form. Add a trust strip with audits-run + sample quote."

Deep SEO audit

12 on-page checks (title, description, canonical, H1, OG, Twitter, JSON-LD, alt coverage, hreflang, robots, viewport, HTTPS) with a per-issue fix.

AI usage audit

Detected AI vendors, model mentions, usage by area (content, search, support, vision, agents…), and prioritized AI opportunities.

METHODOLOGY
How the score is calculated

Deterministic page signals first, AI judgment second — so every recommendation is grounded in something we actually measured on your page.

1. Real browser render

Headless Chromium with JavaScript enabled, waited for the page to settle — so we score what users actually see, not the source HTML.

Loaded in 9.7s · 286 KB · 8 scripts
2. Deterministic signals

Pulled from the rendered page so the AI cannot contradict them.

title.length: 58
description.length: 142
h1.count: 1 · h2.count: 7
canonical.selfReferencing: false
images.missingAlt: 0
jsonLd.types: [WebApplication]
3. Grounded AI scoring

The model scores each category 0–100 and writes recommendations using those signals as ground truth, citing copy from the page.

"canonical present but not self-referencing — weakens canonical clarity." (cites canonical.selfReferencing: false)
Why this beats asking ChatGPT to "review my landing page"
GENERIC AI
— Hallucinates page content it never saw
— Invents stats ("studies show 40% bounce rate…")
— No structure: vague, repetitive recommendations
— Can't tell if the canonical is self-referencing
THIS AUDITOR
+ Renders the page in a real browser first
+ Extracts ~30 deterministic signals before scoring
+ Same rubric every run, scored 0–100 per category
+ Recommendations cite the actual page and ranked by impact

ABOUT
Why this auditor exists

Most "AI website reviewers" are a thin wrapper over a chat prompt. They never load your page, they invent stats, and the recommendations are the same five generic bullets every time.

This tool was built the opposite way. Every audit renders the URL in a real headless browser, extracts ~30 deterministic signals from the rendered HTML, and only then asks an AI model to score and write recommendations — with the signals as ground truth. If the canonical is broken, we know it. If there are zero product images above the fold, we know it. The model can't hand-wave around it.

It's also self-audited: this homepage has been run through its own auditor 1,139+ times, and every recommendation it surfaced has either been shipped or has a clear reason it wasn't. The visible URL label you're reading right now? That was a recommendation from run #32.

BUILT ON

OpenAI gpt-5.4 (JSON mode)

No signup. URLs you submit are stored so you (and others) can re-open the report. Don't paste anything you wouldn't want public.
